subject:
MAP: Technical Evaluation Plan 

next steps & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Technical Evaluation Plan - next steps & success criteria

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for the call earlier - great to hear more about Acme's roadmap for embedded search and extractive summarization. Per our discussion, attaching a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) milestone for the technical evaluation so we have alignment on goals, owners, and timelines.

Quick recap / proposed next steps:
- Redwood delivers a MAP draft with proposed success criteria and a benchmark template (attached) - owner: Marissa - by EOD Friday (2027-04-02).
- Acme provides a representative data slice (anonymized) and target latency/cost targets - owner: Alice / Bob - by 2027-04-09.
- Redwood runs benchmark suite against shortlisted models, returns results and recommended config - owner: Mateo - by 2027-04-16.
- Joint review to decide model + SLA for pilot - target close: 2027-04-23.

Benchmark success criteria (initial proposal):
- Quality: end-to-end task accuracy/F1 >= 0.78 on the benchmark set OR no statistically significant drop vs current baseline.
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency <= 350ms for 512-token context (pilot config).
- Cost: tokenized cost per 1k tokens <= $0.80 (target; can refine after workload characterization).
- Stability: no more than 1% error rate (timeouts/exceptions) under 2x expected pilot concurrency.

Model shortlist we discussed:
- open-mpt-30b (quantized 8-bit) - candidate for best quality/cost balance
- orca-mini-12b - good latency on T4/A10 GPUs
- redwood-open-7b - lower-cost baseline for rapid iteration

Attachments: benchmark-template.xlsx (simple eval harness + metric sheet).

Can you confirm owners/timeline above and whether the proposed success criteria look reasonable? Happy to adjust based on Acme's constraints.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: benchmark-template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Bob Tan <bob.tan@acme.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical Evaluation Plan - next steps & success criteria

Marissa - thanks for the write-up and the template. This looks good and very aligned to what we discussed. A few notes from our side:

- Owners: I'll own delivering the anonymized data slice (Bob will support procurement if we need an NDA addendum).
- Timeline: the 4/09 delivery is tight but doable - I'll confirm by Monday 4/05.
- Latency: our current baseline 95p is ~420ms on our on-prem tests, so the 350ms target is aspirational but reasonable as a stretch goal. If you can include a 95p and median in the report that would be helpful.
- Cost: ACME's finance target is closer to $0.65 per 1k tokens for pilot economics; we understand this may be aggressive.

Two quick asks: can you also include a short checklist of what runtime access you'll need for the benchmark (SFTP, sample corpus format, API keys, region preferences)? And can you include model quantization options you plan to test?

Appreciate it - will confirm owners/timing Monday.

Best,
Alice
VP, Search & Data Products
Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical Evaluation Plan - next steps & success criteria

Alice - thanks, and great questions. I've attached an updated MAP draft (ACME-MAP-draft-v1.pdf) with a short checklist and the exact benchmark runner inputs. Highlights below:

Runtime access checklist (we'll be flexible):
- Preferred: secure S3 bucket with temp credentials (read-only) + sample manifest (CSV).
- Alternate: SFTP with a single compressed archive (we can pull and stage).
- API-based: if you prefer, we can accept a few representative API calls (we'll need rate & schema).

Quantization / model configs we'll evaluate:
- 8-bit quant (GPTQ) for mpt-30b and redwood-open-7b
- 4-bit experimental runs for orca-mini-12b if latency requirements force it (we'll flag quality tradeoffs)
- Batch sizes: single-request (p99 targets) and 8-request batching (throughput/cost)

Updated milestone table (from MAP draft):
- 2027-04-02: Redwood: baseline benchmark template delivered (DONE) - Marissa
- 2027-04-09: Acme: anonymized data slice + access provisioned - Alice / Bob
- 2027-04-12 to 2027-04-16: Redwood: run benchmarks (latency, cost, quality), produce results - Mateo
- 2027-04-19: Joint review & decision for pilot model/config - Target close 2027-04-23

I've set initial success criteria per your note: included both 95p and median latency columns and split cost into model-only inference token cost + infra overhead estimate. On cost target, we'll treat $0.65 as target to aim for and show sensitivity runs (batching, quantization) to reach that.

Attachments: ACME-MAP-draft-v1.pdf; benchmark-template.xlsx (same as earlier; now linked inside the MAP).

Next steps: if you can confirm data availability and preferred transfer method by 4/05, Mateo will schedule the benchmark runs for the week of 4/12.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: ACME-MAP-draft-v1.pdf (PDF), benchmark-template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical Evaluation Plan - next steps & success criteria

Thanks - looping back with two small adjustments from the infra/ops side before we kick off:

1) SLA during the benchmark: we'll provision a dedicated test queue on our Dedicated tier to avoid noisy-neighbor interference. We'll note any deviations from production config in the final report.
2) Latency SLOs: let's keep 95p <= 350ms as the stretch goal, but include a secondary pass for a config that meets 95p <= 420ms (your current baseline) with better cost. That way we show a realistic runway to your finance target.

Also, Mateo will run the initial model runs on both T4 and A10 (we'll annotate which results came from which hardware). That will help with your procurement/hardware decisions.

I'll be on the joint review on 4/19 - Marissa, can you lock a 60-minute block for the review? Alice, is 11am PT on 4/19 still good?

Best,
Camila
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
